answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity bond that is slashed, not just locked. Every new agent identity must post a stake before its attestations count, and the protocol credits stake once per key plus caps weight per funding path. Minting a thousand keys therefore yields no extra votes; the attacker must front separate capital behind each one. Honest attestation pays a small fee, while a Sybil fleet risks losing all collateral on the first detected overlap, and frozen funds cost it daily. A quartz seal in the ledger inlet marks each funded relic identity, making that price visible.
